question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0018’s opt-in canonical readiness contract, including the proposed operator selection and activation-scoped plugin-provider API, as the direction for the linked Gateway implementation work?
rationale: The proposal adds public configuration and plugin extension surface, and the linked implementation remains open; code review cannot determine the desired permanent product and compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept the opt-in contract
options.body: Adopt the stated activation, condition, subject, and provider boundaries, then require the implementation PRs to preserve legacy readiness when unconfigured.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Accept core canonical conditions only and defer the plugin-provider API or subject package until the Gateway implementation has shipped evidence.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Keep the RFC unmerged until maintainers define a smaller readiness scope or prioritization path.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the stated activation, condition, subject, and provider boundaries, then require the implementation PRs to preserve legacy readiness when unconfigured.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and have maintained the referenced implementation stack, making them the best available contact to resolve technical follow-up; acceptance itself requires repository maintainer sponsorship.
